_comment: Alert rules as data, not branches -- the same choice levers.json makes,
for the same reason: which conditions are worth waking somebody for is a
merchant's decision, not ours, and it should not need a deploy.
Each rule watches ONE metric off the live schedule. The schedule is the
same compute_schedule the dashboard renders, so an alert can never
disagree with what an operator sees on screen.
cooldown_minutes is measured in SIMULATED time (app/clock.py), so a run
at 25x compresses it exactly as it compresses everything else. It is the
spam guard AND the budget guard: every firing sends one email per
matching recipient, against a 300/day allowance shared with signup and
A rule fires when it matches and its cooldown has elapsed -- OR when the
situation has escalated above the level last alerted on, which bypasses
the cooldown. Waiting out a cooldown while MEDIUM becomes CRITICAL is the
one silence that would actually cost an operator something.
telemetry-gone-quiet has a deliberately long cooldown: a simulator left
off overnight would otherwise email the whole list every few minutes,
and the second reminder tells an operator nothing the first did not.
Every number here is a demo default, not business truth.

rules.name: The floor has stopped reporting
rules.subject: SurgeGuard: no telemetry from {facility_id} for {snapshot_age_minutes:.0f} minutes
rules.body:
{facility_id} has not reported fulfillment progress for about {snapshot_age_minutes:.0f} minutes.

Until it does, the risk picture is a guess: with no fresh throughput the scheduler falls back to the facility's configured capacity, which means the dashboard will look BETTER than the floor actually is, not worse.

Check that the fulfillment feed is still running before trusting anything else on the dashboard.

rules.name: Promises already missed
rules.subject: SurgeGuard: {breached_count} missed promises at {facility_id}
rules.body:
{breached_count} orders at {facility_id} have passed their promised dispatch time, with {at_risk_count} more at risk.

These are already late. No lever recovers them -- the decision now is whether the customers hear it from us first.

Open the recovery view to see what each option trades.

rules.name: Facility at critical risk
rules.subject: SurgeGuard: {facility_id} at CRITICAL risk
rules.body:
{facility_id} is at CRITICAL risk: {at_risk_count} orders at risk and {breached_count} already breached, against {pending_orders} pending.

Open the recovery view to compare what each option actually prevents.

rules.name: Decision window closing
rules.subject: SurgeGuard: {minutes_to_first_breach:.0f} minutes to the first breach at {facility_id}
rules.body:
The first promise at {facility_id} fails in about {minutes_to_first_breach:.0f} minutes.

Levers that take longer than that to land will not rescue it. The recovery view marks those as unavailable rather than offering them.

rules.name: Backlog growing faster than the floor clears it
rules.subject: SurgeGuard: backlog outpacing throughput at {facility_id}
rules.body:
Work is arriving at {facility_id} about {backlog_growth_wu_per_hour:.0f} work units per hour faster than the floor is clearing it.

Nothing has breached yet. Acting while that is still true is the cheapest this decision ever gets.
